descriptionChirho: The noun καταβολή in its dominant cosmological sense, meaning 'foundation, laying down, beginning,' used almost exclusively in the phrase 'foundation of the world' (καταβολὴ κόσμου) referring to the creation or establishment of the world. Attested 10x in the NT (Matt 13:35; 25:34; Luke 11:50; John 17:24; Eph 1:4; Heb 4:3; 9:26; 1 Pet 1:20; Rev 13:8; 17:8). Multilingual evidence: Spanish 'fundación,' Hindi 'नींव/स्थापना' (foundation/establishment), Arabic 'تأسيس' (founding), Korean '창조/창세' (creation/beginning of the world), Swahili 'mwanzo/kuwekwa msingi' (beginning/laying of foundation).

The noun καταβολή in its biological-reproductive sense, meaning 'conception, depositing of seed,' referring to the act of conceiving offspring. Attested 1x in the NT (Heb 11:11), where Sarah receives power 'for the depositing of seed' (εἰς καταβολὴν σπέρματος). This draws on the etymological meaning of καταβάλλω ('to throw/cast down, deposit'). Multilingual evidence clearly differentiates this from the cosmological sense: Hindi 'गर्भ धारण' (conception/pregnancy), Arabic 'إلقاء' (casting/depositing), Korean '창조를' (shows some overlap), Spanish 'fundación' (less differentiated), Swahili 'kupata' (to receive/obtain). The biological specificity marks this as a distinct lexicographic sense.
